title: Late Arrival
statement: A clinic keeps today's appointment times (minutes after opening) as a linked list in increasing order. A patient books one more time, `time`. Insert a new node with that time so the list stays in increasing order, and return the head. If the time is already in the list, put the new node after the existing ones.
constraints: The list is in increasing order

answerKey.pattern: Dummy node, walk to the last node that is not later, then link the new node in
keyPoints: A dummy node in front handles inserting before the head
Move prev forward while prev.next exists and prev.next.val <= time
Create the node and set node.next = prev.next, then prev.next = node, in that order
edgeCases: Equal times already in the list
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Copy to an array, insert, and rebuild the list: O(n) extra space

hints: Where does the new node go: after which node?
Walk prev from a dummy node while the next time is not later than the new one.
Link the new node to prev.next before you change prev.next, or you lose the rest of the list.
